meta.title: mechanisms inside a laser-cut animatronic talking head
meta.author: Shasa Bolton

blocks.text: Mechanisms Inside a Laser-cut Animatronic Talking Head

blocks.content: My journey into mechanical curiosities, actually started with animatronics. The first one I built was a comissioned fudge making woman for a cafe. This was an elaborate time consuming project which involved moulding the cafe owners face and casting a silicone copy of her. Each eye was hung on a universal joint with 2 servo motors pulling it left/right and up/down. The eyebrows each had cables attached to servo motors to move each end of the eyebrow up and down. Her head also sat on a universal joint with two rods at the back controling tilt and nod. This mechanism then sat on a side to side neck pivot. She had a servo in her jaw and a motor driving a spoon to make her hand stir her fudge pot sympathetically. She was controlled by an arduino with an mp3 sheild for the audio files, an SD card sheild for the animation data, a servo driver board, IR sensors to detect coins, an amplifier, speakers and multiple power supplies. To animate her I wrote some custom sorftware that consisted of vistual joysticks on my screen. These moved the servos when the arduino was plugged in over usb. I could press reccord and have all my movements reccorded and stored for playback from the sd card later. I prefered this to key frames which can look very robotic. Most parts were custom made by hand. Machined aluminium, pvc pipe, rod ends and linkages, cast resin underskull and silicone skin. I loved the process, but finished feeling a little vulnerable as to how bespoke repairs would be, and how time consuming it would be to make it all again for the next project. I also had no way to see what was happening inside the arduino without have a laptop nearby.  At this stage, I had no 3d printer, laser cutter or router so the design was not based on automatable manufacture. I went on to build other talking heads, birds and tentacles. All still bespoke hand made designs. All controled by arduinos with mp3 shields, separate servo controlers and custom animation software for each design. The pain of feeling that my designs relied on me for their survival lead me to move towards a strong focus on a one material, one machine, automatable design philosophy. What followed was a long exploration of 100% laser cut wooden mechanism. All hand cranked and free from electronics or software. If a part needed replacing its blueprint lived like DNA in the svg files and could quickly be laser cut by anyone. I then returned to animatronics, with this minimalist approach at hand. I set out to once again make a talking head. But this time I wanted to use nothing but the servo motors and laser cut parts. No rod ends, bearings, casting, soldering or precice hand made components. I also did not want multiple circuit boards that all needed to speak each others language and have firmware compiled and flashed at every small development. So here is what I made. An animatronic kit that can be made by anyone. It is designed as a sort of layered 2 dimensional mask. The mouth and eyes slide within a track. The eyerows pivot about their center and are also driven by a sliding rack. There are no linkages or cables. The 9g micro servos simply use their standard arms and their own mounting screw fitted so that it pushes against slots in the wooden mechanisms. For the electronics, I moved most of the hardware to your phone. The speaker, logic, sensors, microphone, camera, touchscreen, internet connection and AI converation all live in your phone. I built a web app that plays the audio and sends live servo motor comands over bluetooth to the robots microcontoler. The microntroller is a simple esp32 board with built in power distribution to the servos. All t does is establishes conection to your phone, receive the live motor comands and sned them to the servos. Any extra functionality I decide I want is now added in the web app and available instantly to any robot that uses it. I designed the circuit board in easy EDA and have it fully manufactured by PCB way or JLC PCB. I can now just use this one circuitboard, powered from a usb phone charger. No more mp3 sheilds, wiring harnesses and servo controller boards. With the control now living on the phone, we have access to all its hardware and can build complex behavior into the web app without needing to update the robots firmware. Rather than animating the character as I did traditionaly, I let it animate it self. The mouth is now syncs with the audio directly in the app rather than matching it by hand or using a separate volume envelope circuitboard.  The eyes track the person in front of it as it can now see their face. The eybrows currently move randomly but there is scope to add some emotion linking algorithm based on the text being spoken. That brings me to how I tackeld my next frustration with animatronics. I always know what they are going to say to me. But now by using a web app, it was very easy to add conversational abilities to the animatronic. The microphone now sends what you say away for AI transcription. The transcript gets sent to an LLM for a response. This response then gets turned into voice with another text to speach AI model. I started off by just having a character bio prompt that shapes how they resond to you. But I realised this was limiting if I wanted to create engineered interactions such as a game of 20 questions or a fortune reading. Chat history needed to be sent with each prompt else the LLM would have know idea what was happening. But we also want to clear chat history at chosen times to save on AI tokens. I wired it up so characters still have their bio, but they also have games they play. Those games are a collection of promtps that outline the game rules. Eg "Give a fortune reading and use real cold reading techniques." You can set triggers so the prompt is only sent when you want. eg After 10 back and forth questions send a prompt that says, "You now have enough information. Wrap up the fortune with a grand finale". I created a few characters and games that are built into the app, but also made it possible for people to write there own. They can choose a voice, white a bio and create game prompts. I am sure this app will evolve as people use it and ask for additional features. For now I think it is a good base for creating varied interactions with animatronic characters. People are welcome to build their own faces that sit over the servo motors. In time I will also create more face plates and have them available for purchase as kits or download.
